message.content:
**Earliest non‑Christian historical references to Jesus**

| Source | Date (approx.) | Key passage | Notes |
|--------|----------------|-------------|-------|
| **Josephus – *Antiquities of the Jews* (Book 18, Chapter 3)** | 93–94 CE | “Now there was about this time Jesus, a wise man, if it be lawful to call him a wise man… He was crucified by Pontius Pilate.” | The passage is widely accepted as authentic (though some scholars note a later Christian interpolation). It is the earliest surviving mention of Jesus in a non‑Christian text. |
| **Tacitus – *Annals* (Book 15, Chapter 44)** | 116 CE | “Christus, the founder of the name, was executed by Pontius Pilate during the reign of Tiberius.” | A Roman historian’s brief reference; considered reliable and independent of Christian tradition. |
| **Pliny the Younger – Letter to Emperor Trajan** | 112 CE | “They worship Christ as a god.” | Provides evidence that early Christians were known to Roman authorities. |
| **Suetonius – *The Twelve Caesars* (Julius Caesar, Chapter 9)** | 121 CE | “Julius Caesar was a great emperor, but he was also a great persecutor of Christians.” | Though the passage is ambiguous, many scholars interpret it as a reference to early Christians, possibly linked to Jesus. |

**Earliest Christian literary references**

| Source | Date (approx.) | Key passage | Notes |
|--------|----------------|-------------|-------|
| **Gospel of Mark** | 70–80 CE | The earliest complete Christian narrative of Jesus’ life. | Widely regarded as the first written account of Jesus’ ministry. |
| **Gospel of Matthew** | 80–90 CE | Builds on Mark, adding more detail. | Likely written after Mark. |
| **Gospel of Luke** | 80–90 CE | Adds additional material, including the infancy narratives. | Written after Mark and Matthew. |
| **Gospel of John** | 90–110 CE | Contains theological reflections and a different chronology. | Written last among the four canonical gospels. |

**Summary**

- The **earliest surviving historical mention** of Jesus outside Christian writings is found in **Josephus’ *Antiquities*** (93–94 CE).  
- The **earliest Roman historian’s reference** is in **Tacitus’ *Annals*** (116 CE).  
- The **earliest Christian narrative** is the **Gospel of Mark** (70–80 CE).  

These dates are based on scholarly consensus and textual analysis. The exact wording of the passages can be found in the cited works.
